title: Bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, and analgesic activity of ketamine in humans

claims.statement: In healthy volunteers given single analgesic amounts in crossover laboratory studies, how much of a ketamine dose reaches the bloodstream depends on the route. Measured against an intravenous dose in the same people, an intramuscular injection gave 93% (0.930, SE 0.026) and a swallowed solution 16.6% (0.166, SE 0.028), each the mean of four people, with a second calculation on all six people giving 19.5% (0.195, SE 0.028) for the swallowed solution (Clements et al., 1982). A later study of three men found 18.3% (SD 4.7) and 17.6% (SD 3.8), for the two mirror-image forms, after a swallowed tablet (Yanagihara et al., 2003), so the oral figure has been found twice by different groups; the intramuscular figure has not been measured again in the sources read here. Blood levels rose fast after the intramuscular injection (peak 243 ng/mL, SE 49, at 22 minutes, SE 4; ketamine present in under 4 minutes; peaks between 100 and 425 ng/mL across people) and stayed low after the swallowed solution (peak 44 ng/mL, SE 10, range 15 to 80, at 30 minutes, SE 5). The 1982 abstract says the oral loss was a failure to absorb, while its own discussion argues that absorption from the gut was complete and the drug was broken down in the liver before reaching the circulation; the metabolite figures in the same paper support the discussion. Both headline figures rest on four people, the intravenous reference is described in a separate five-person study without saying who provided it, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in either paper.
claims.magnitude: Clements et al. (1982): intramuscular Farea 0.930 (SE 0.026, n=4 printed values 0.965, 0.923, 0.972, 0.859); oral Farea 0.166 (SE 0.028, n=4: 0.145, 0.163, 0.112, 0.245) and 0.195 (SE 0.028) from Eq. 2 across 6 people; intramuscular Cmax 243 ng/mL (SE 49) at tmax 22 min (SE 4); oral Cmax 44 ng/mL (SE 10) at 30 min (SE 5). Yanagihara et al. (2003), swallowed tablet in 3 men: bioavailability 18.3% (SD 4.7) for the (R)- and 17.6% (SD 3.8) for the (S)-enantiomer; Cmax 42.6 (SD 13.3) and 40.4 (SD 14.2) ng/mL at 33.3 (SD 15.3) and 30.0 (SD 30.0) min.

claims.statement: After a single intravenous amount in healthy volunteers, blood ketamine falls in two phases, fast at first and then over a few hours. In 1982 the terminal half-life was 186 minutes (standard error 10 in the text and 8 in the table) and total clearance 19.1 mL/min/kg; the half-life after an intramuscular injection, 155 minutes (SE 12), and after a swallowed solution, 174 minutes (SE 50), did not differ significantly from it (Clements et al., 1982). In three men in 2003 the terminal half-life after an intravenous injection was 126.8 minutes (SD 47.4) for the (R)- and 117.3 minutes (SD 47.9) for the (S)-form, with clearance 1.1 and 1.2 L/h/kg, and no half-life is printed for any of that study's other preparations (Yanagihara et al., 2003). A 2016 review gives, second-hand, a distribution half-life of 2 to 4 minutes and an elimination half-life of 2 to 4 hours, with 4 to 7 hours for S-ketamine. The body turns ketamine into norketamine: the review reports that about 80% is converted, that norketamine appears in plasma 2 to 3 minutes after an intravenous injection and peaks at 30 to 60 minutes, and that recent work indicates norketamine is itself broken down quickly and may not be the main substance circulating. Norketamine was measurable after every route in 1982, with peaks of 40 ng/mL (SE 6) after the intravenous, 92 (SE 10) after the intramuscular and 200 (SE 44) after the oral condition, while the dose-corrected areas (35.4, 31.3 and 36.7) were similar, which the authors read as showing that a swallowed dose is absorbed and then broken down in the liver before reaching the circulation. How long ketamine lasts after being swallowed, taken under the tongue, given rectally or sprayed into the nose is not reported in either study.
claims.magnitude: Clements et al. (1982): intravenous terminal half-life 186 min (SE 10 in the Results, SE 8 in Table II), clearance 19.1 mL/min/kg (SE 1.1); intramuscular 155 min (SE 12) and 23.2 mL/min/kg (SE 2.7); oral 174 min (SE 50). Norketamine peaks 40 (SE 6), 92 (SE 10) and 200 ng/mL (SE 44) at 63, 78 and 60 min, dose-corrected areas 35.4 (3.8), 31.3 (3.8) and 36.7 (3.9), described as not significantly different. Yanagihara et al. (2003), intravenous, n=3: 126.8 min (SD 47.4) for (R)- and 117.3 (SD 47.9) for (S)-ketamine; area 138.0 (15.6) and 126.3 (15.1) ng·h/mL; clearance 1.1 (0.2) and 1.2 (0.1) L/h/kg; steady-state volume of distribution 2.5 L/kg. Peltoniemi et al. (2016), second-hand: distribution half-life 2–4 min, elimination 2–4 h (S-ketamine 4–7 h), about 80% converted to norketamine.
